form.title: Qualified Adoption Expenses
form.notes: refundable: mixed, and this is NEW FOR 2025. P.L. 119-21 made part of the adoption credit refundable for tax years beginning after December 31, 2024. Line 13 is the REFUNDABLE adoption credit and goes to Form 1040 line 30 — a line that read 'Reserved for future use' on the 2024 Form 1040 and now carries a caption naming this form. Line 18 is the NONREFUNDABLE adoption credit and goes to Schedule 3 Part I line 6c. Line 31 is neither: it is taxable employer-provided adoption benefits and lands in income on Form 1040 line 1f. 2025 parameters read off the form's own face and confirmed against Rev. Proc. 2024-40 section 2.04: maximum credit and maximum exclusion $17,280 per child (lines 2 and 19); MAGI phase-out begins at $259,190 over a $40,000 range, so it is fully phased out at $299,190 (lines 8, 9, 26 and 27); the REFUNDABLE portion is capped at $5,000 per child (line 11b). The Instructions for Form 8839 (2025) add two limits the form encodes structurally rather than prints: 'Unused nonrefundable credit can't be turned into a refundable credit in a future year' and 'Any amount of the carryforward credit from 2024 remains a nonrefundable credit.' The form enforces both by bringing prior-year carryforward in at line 15, only AFTER line 13 has taken the refundable piece out at line 14. Unused nonrefundable credit carries forward 'to the next 5 years or until used, whichever comes first.' P.L. 119-21 also amended section 23(d)(3) to recognise a determination by an Indian tribal government, not only a State, that a child has special needs — the Form 8839 What's New calls this 'Parity for Indian tribal governments.' Printed revision: Form 8839 (2025), Created 9/2/25.
